- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- If model shows a sharp upward trend (e.g., >0.5% daily increase) after a dip, it often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- When true outcome spikes >10% from prior 5-day average, model often fails to catch it; add 1–2 days of lagged spike correction (e.g., if true rises 15%, forecast should start rising 12–14% from prior).
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7–14 days.
- Model often underestimates mean reversion after strong spikes; if true outcome drops >5% from peak, forecast should reflect 3–5 day mean reversion trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-cycle corrections; add 1–2 days of downward bias if sentiment turns negative or true outcome shows early correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2–0.3 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply 0.5–1.0% dampening to forecast slope for next 7 days.
